correctness.rationale: The K5-free extension test is exhaustive: forbidden K5 configurations involve either one new vertex with a K4 old neighborhood (excluded type), or both adjacent new vertices with a common old triangle. The hereditary Boolean zeta matrix is unitriangular, so the displayed exact integer congruence and coefficients follow from finite Möbius inversion. The standalone C++17 checker exhausts every labelled graph through seven vertices and isolates precisely 420 labelled wheel representations. Its degree and K4 checks prove one isomorphism class, not merely a numerical witness. A separate Python 3 checker exactly constructs the 128x128 wheel matrix, performs integer row/column finite differences, and recovers 22 units, one 2 and 105 zeros. No infinite claim follows from the census; only the symbolic identity is all-size.

A known model-theoretic extension criterion and general incidence-Möbius transform do not classify the seven-point coefficient extrema. Historical priority remains provisional because an unindexed Euler-characteristic table might imply the finite statement.

value.rationale: The natural first nonunit Smith factor measures the earliest characteristic-dependent loss of adjacency-feasibility rank between nonalgebraic types in a homogeneous forbidden-clique structure. The sharp cutoff at seven individually named parameters and uniqueness of the 6-rim wheel are motivated extremal invariants; the order-two factor distinguishes this K5-free setting from earlier K4-free odd-torsion and unit Smith results. The result is not only a one-off matrix computation, because it rules out every other finite parameter base through the first occurrence.
